newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Hoyts sees no new issues this year.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Hoyts sees no new issues this year.

text.p: Cinema operator Hoyts Cinemas Group Ltd said on Thursday that it was unlikely to have any more equity raisings in the current 1996/97 year unless a very large opportunity arose.

"Yes, that's enough for everything on our plate at the moment," Hoyts chief financial officer Colin Resnick told reporters after the annual general meeting, when asked if a A$61.1 million capital raising announced earlier would be the last for the current year.

Earlier Hoyts said the A$61.1 million placement would be used to fund the A$28 million purchase of a 35 percent interest in Mexican cinema operator Cinemex and other acquisitions and developments this year.
Hoyts chief executive Peter Ivany said Hoyts was looking at further acquisitions in north-eastern United States, Latin America and in Western Europe.

He said Hoyts wanted to confine its presence in the United States to the north-eastern region as that is where it already had a strong presence. "The U.S. market is just too big and too competitive, you can't cover it all," Ivany told reporters.
He said Hoyts planned to complete the acquisitions in the first six months of calendar 1997.

Hoyts had to take advantage of a window of opportunity open for the next three to five years in Western Europe and Latin America to find good sites to build new cinema complexes to meet growing demand.

Earlier, Hoyts Chairman David Gonski said Hoyts was finalising a 54 screen acquisition in New Jersey in the United States and Hoyts was either developing or in negotiation to buy an extra 1,500 screens.
Ivany said Hoyts was looking at other opportunities there.
He said Hoyts planned to eventually develop operations in ten countries over the next five years. It currently operates in Australia, New Zealand and the United States.
Hoyts shares were up three cents at A$2.95 at 2.35 p.m. (0435 GMT).
